data.title: China bars Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Xi meet after question on Nvidia
data.description:
It's a scenario seen every day: A reporter shouts a question out to a leader at an event. The leader either answers or ignores it. In China, though, Bloomberg TV journalist Annmarie Hordern was blocked from a key event by Chinese officials, apparently as retribution for having shouted a question in a way that the government considered rude.

Hordern was barred from Thursday's trilateral meeting among President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, after having called out a question during a Trump meeting with Xi. She had asked Trump if former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the United States.

 

A White House official said the Chinese insisted the reporter not be allowed in despite the White House having pushed for admission. The official insisted on speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity around the issue.

The White House did not immediately respond to a query about what steps it took to advocate for the reporter. Jacqui Heinrich, president of the White House Correspondents' Association, said on X that it was "commendable that the WH is advocating for press access".

A pool report from the incident said the Chinese "have passed along a message that yelling questions is considered extremely rude and we will be pulled from the room if we do so".

China's Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press, and an email to Bloomberg seeking comment was not immediately returned.

The incident, which reflected the way China typically seeks to tightly control news events, recalled a previous one in 2022, in which a White House pool reporter said she was knocked off balance after being yanked by her backpack when she tried to shout a question to President Joe Biden. The question was about human rights ahead of a meeting between Biden and Xi in Bali, Indonesia.

The reporter lost balance without falling and was pushed towards the door, a pool report said at the time. Two White House staff members intervened and said the producer should be left alone.

China's approach to journalists, particularly foreign media, has long been chilly and uneven. In recent decades, international reporters have been expelled both for their coverage and for perceived misbehavior during news events. Resident correspondents are occasionally detained and questioned -- and in some cases in past years, compelled to sign "self-criticism" reports -- for showing up where the government doesn't want them to be.

Chinese journalists who stray from the party line can face even more stringent measures, including censorship, dismissal and at times even imprisonment.

data.title: Nvidia stock falls 32% in Nov: Is it a buying opportunity? Analysts answer
data.description:
Nvidia’s sharp share price correction has put the US chipmaker back on the radar of Indian investors, but market experts say the fall alone may not make it an attractive buying opportunity. While the company’s artificial intelligence (AI) business continues to report strong growth, concerns over leadership uncertainty, stretched AI valuations and the sustainability of technology companies’ infrastructure spending have clouded the near-term outlook.
 
Nvidia shares have declined nearly 32 per cent since October 29, when reports surrounding chief executive Jensen Huang first emerged. The stock traded at $213.66 on October 29 and at $145.98 on November 19, a fall of around 31.7 per cent.
 
 
The controversy intensified after reports of Huang’s relationship with a former executive of Nvidia partner Megaspeed International, who was reportedly under scrutiny by US intelligence agencies over suspected links to China. Huang subsequently resigned as chief executive on November 12, with chief financial officer Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO. Nvidia’s board has initiated an independent investigation, while the developments have also drawn regulatory and legal scrutiny.
 
However, analysts caution against attributing the entire decline to the developments around Huang. Concerns about AI valuations, the scale of capital expenditure by major technology companies and the sustainability of future demand for advanced chips were already weighing on the sector.
 
“Nvidia’s correction reflects a combination of factors rather than one development. Concerns around elevated AI valuations, the sustainability of infrastructure spending and broader technology-sector weakness were already weighing on the stock. The developments surrounding Jensen Huang have added another layer of uncertainty, particularly around leadership continuity and strategic relationships,” said Viram Shah, founder and chief executive officer of Vested.
 
Shah said the more important question for investors is whether the developments have a lasting impact on Nvidia’s business execution, customer relationships and earnings growth. 
ALSO READ: On shaky ground: These 11 Indian MFs are most exposed to US tech selloff
 
Nvidia fundamentals remain strong, but valuation matters
 
“Nvidia’s underlying business remains strong despite the uncertainty surrounding its leadership. Its latest quarterly revenue more than doubled year-on-year, while data centre revenue grew approximately 117 per cent, reflecting continued demand for AI infrastructure,” Shah said.
 
He added that Nvidia’s competitive advantage extends beyond its graphics processing units (GPUs) to its software, networking technologies and developer tools, which have made its products deeply integrated into customers’ operations.
 
Vinit Bolinjkar, head of research at Ventura, said Nvidia’s competitive position remains strong, supported by its CUDA software ecosystem, high-performance networking and integrated AI computing platforms. However, the growing availability of custom AI chips and the concentration of revenue among large customers remain key risks.
 
On valuation, Bolinjkar said Nvidia trades at approximately 20 times trailing reported earnings and 13 times forward estimated earnings following the correction. While these multiples appear more attractive relative to the company’s growth profile, investors need to assess whether earnings growth can be sustained.
 
The correction, therefore, should not automatically be seen as a buying opportunity, he said. 
ALSO READ: AI trade unwinds; India emerges as a diversification opportunity: Brokerage
 
Should Indian investors buy Nvidia shares?
 
For Indian investors looking to gain exposure to the global AI theme, Nvidia remains a significant company to track. However, analysts recommend a staggered investment approach rather than attempting to time the bottom.
 
“Nvidia remains an important company in the global AI ecosystem, and the long-term opportunity in AI infrastructure continues to be significant. For Indian investors, the recent correction could offer an opportunity to evaluate the stock at a more reasonable valuation, provided the underlying business outlook remains intact,” Shah said.
 
He added that Nvidia should be part of a diversified global portfolio rather than a standalone bet on AI. Investors should also account for technology-sector concentration and currency movements.
 
Bolinjkar also favoured a staggered approach, particularly until there is greater clarity on management succession and future earnings guidance. He said the leadership transition and uncertainty surrounding the profitability of global AI investments could keep the stock volatile.
 
Meanwhile, Sidharth Sogani Jain, Founder, CEO & Fund Manager at Blue Aster Capital said buy Nvidia but, “in stages rather than in one go. I'd cap it at 5–10 per cent of equity holdings. Indian investors also carry rupee risk, US regulatory risk and the concentration risk of a single stock.”
 
How can Indian investors buy Nvidia shares?
 
Indian residents can access Nvidia shares directly through overseas brokerage platforms under the Reserve Bank of India’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS). They can also gain indirect exposure through international mutual funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that hold the stock, subject to availability and applicable investment limits.

data.title: Cyberattack leaks JPMorgan Chase customer emails, some phone numbers
data.description:
Personal information belonging to thousands of JPMorgan Chase customers was leaked onto the internet after third-party vendors at the bank were targeted in a cyberattack. The leak is unrelated to a bank outage earlier this week and the information involved did not include credit card or particularly sensitive personal information, the bank said.

The leaked data appears to be mostly email addresses of Chase customers as well as some bank employees, as well as their phone numbers in some cases.

"We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack," said Joe Evangelisti, a spokesperson for the bank on Thursday.

 

Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.

Visa and Mastercard also confirmed the data breach, but the hack had no impact on company functions or customer payment information.

The accounts impacted, which number in the thousands, are a fraction of Chase's customer base. Chase has tens of millions of customers and Visa and Mastercard have billions of customers.

"At this time, the exposure has been contained and our teams are working with the provider to support the impacted cardholders as needed," said Seth Eisen, a spokesperson for Mastercard.

The cyber attack was an unrelated incident to what happened with Chase earlier this week, when a software bug caused outages in some of Chase's banking services.

However, this cyber attack is the latest in a series of technological problems that has hit various parts of the global economy, with flights being grounded to basic email and calendar services from Microsoft being not operational.

data.title: Cyclone Akvan: Odisha evacuates over 300K people, 47 trains cancelled
data.description:
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi conducted another comprehensive review of the preparedness and response measures for the impending Cyclone 'Akvan'.

​According to the official release, detailed discussions were held regarding cyclone readiness.

All necessary steps are being taken in close coordination among the state administration, district administrations, and concerned Central Government departments to achieve the 'Zero Casualty' target. Expressing strong confidence, the Chief Minister stated that with the blessings of Mahaprabhu Shri Jagannath, this goal will certainly be accomplished.

​Briefing the media following the review meeting, the Chief Minister informed that according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Cyclone 'Akvan' is likely to make landfall on Friday afternoon at Haripur, near Gopalpur.

 

​Extensive preparedness and mitigation measures have been undertaken across 20 districts of the state to tackle the situation.

​So far, more than 300,000 people have been evacuated to safe locations. Additionally, 4,170 pregnant women have been shifted to safe shelters, out of whom 1,317 women have given birth to newborn babies, the Chief Minister stated.

​While a total of 9,341 cyclone shelters have been kept ready across the state, 2,623 of them have already been made operational.

​For rapid field-level response, a total of 418 teams have been deployed. These include 60 ODRAF teams, 14 NDRF teams, 216 Fire Service teams, and 128 tree-cutting teams from the Odisha Forest Development Corporation (OFDC). Furthermore, an additional 28 Fire Service teams have been kept on standby.

​To ensure uninterrupted telecommunication during the cyclone, arrangements have been made for 17 satellite phones, Cells on Wheels (CoW), and telecom backup systems.

​Meanwhile, through ORSAC, a total of 941 landslide-prone villages have been identified across 6 districts- Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Kandhamal, Malkangiri, and Koraput. Arrangements have been put in place to evacuate residents from these villages to safer locations. Most of the people evacuated in Kandhamal and Gajapati districts belong to these landslide-prone areas.

​Responding to media queries regarding some fishermen from Andhra Pradesh stranded near the Odisha coast, the Chief Minister said that all arrangements have been made for their safety with the assistance of the Indian Coast Guard, and steps are underway to bring them safely to Ganjam district.

​During the review, the Chief Minister spoke over the phone with the Puri District Collector to inquire about the ground situation and preparedness, advising him to pay special attention to the safety of the Habishyalis (elderly women observing Kartika rituals).

​The Chief Minister also informed that 47 trains have been cancelled, and 28 trains have been rescheduled.

​Clarifying that the Coast Guard and the Rail Coordination Cell remain active for emergency rescue operations, the Chief Minister reiterated that all departments are on high alert and fully prepared, giving top priority to the safety of the people of the state.

​Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari was present during the review meeting. Chief Secretary Anu Garg, Additional Chief Secretary (Revenue Department) Arabinda Padhee, Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil, along with Principal Secretaries and Secretaries of various departments, were also in attendance.

data.title: Trump's cyber chief Sean Cairncross to step down amid repeated tech outages
data.description:
In what is being described as a direct fallout of the consistent outages plaguing tech services in the US, President Donald Trump's National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is stepping down from his post, Fox News has confirmed.

His departure comes following disruptions involving Microsoft Outlook, United Airlines, major banks and the NSA, along with a nationwide FAA ground stop. Fox News cited an official who said that Cairncross does not want to serve another two years in the role, though his departure date remains unclear.

Caincross' reported exit came despite Trump urging Americans not to panic or stockpile emergency supplies following a string of high-profile technology and banking disruptions across the United States, insisting the incidents are isolated technical glitches rather than a coordinated cyberattack.

 

Speaking in an interview with Fox News ahead of the APEC Summit, Trump was asked about growing public anxiety, including reports of people stockpiling food and water, prompted by the recent outages and his earlier declaration of a national emergency over the US power grid.

The president brushed off the concerns, characterising the disruptions at major institutions like JPMorgan Chase as routine, unrelated occurrences amplified by media coverage.

"Tell them to relax. Everything's good. These are individual events. So, Chase Manhattan Bank, JPMorgan, it goes out. Somebody else goes out. And I also think that, the press is sort of having a lot of fun with it," Trump said.

On Thursday, JPMorgan Chase disclosed that third-party service providers working with the financial institution were targeted in a cyberattack, with reports indicating that data, including email addresses and phone numbers, belonging to around 16,000 of its wealthy customers was exposed by a ransomware group.

According to Fox News, a ransomware group identified as non-profit claimed responsibility for leaking data belonging to customers of JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard.

The breach reportedly involved third-party business partners and exposed customer email addresses, phone numbers and account IDs.

In a post on X, JPMorgan on Thursday (local time) said it had learned that third parties providing services to the firm had been targeted in a cyberattack. The bank said its investigation suggested that attackers had accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may have included customer names and email addresses.

The latest incidents involving JPMorgan come amid several other technology-related disruptions in recent weeks, including a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that affected air travel last week and a global email outage at Microsoft. Last month, cryptocurrency exchange Binance also experienced a major cyberattack.

data.title: Newly-listed companies add ₹32-trillion to BSE market-cap in 2026
data.description:
Jio Platforms, the recently listed Reliance Group telecom services company, the National Stock Exchange (NSE), ICICI Asset Management Company (AMC), Meesho and SBI Funds Management are among nearly 300 companies that helped add ₹32 trillion in the total market capitalisation (market-cap) of the BSE listed companies since December 2025.
 
The total market cap of BSE-listed companies hit a record high of ₹512.27 trillion on November 12, 2026. On Thursday, November 19, the BSE-listed companies' market cap stood at ₹511.97 trillion, exchange data shows.
 
The market cap of the BSE-listed companies stood at ₹474.53 trillion on December 1, 2025, when BSE Sensex hit a record high of 86,159.02. The benchmark index hit an intraday high of 83,043.87 on Thursday, which is 3.75 per cent or 3,115.15 points away from its all-time high level.
 
 
According to CaptialinePlus database, 299 companies listed since December 2025, added Rs 31.59 trillion to the total market-cap of the BSE listed companies. 
ALSO READ: RIL stock in focus: What next after near 12% surge? Analyst decodes history
 
Of these, Jio Platforms alone contributed 41 per cent or ₹12.85 trillion in market cap, while NSE accounted for a 17 per cent or 5.42 trillion addition to the total market-cap of the BSE-listed companies. ICICI AMC added ₹1.46 trillion, followed by Meesho (₹1.2 trillion), SBI Funds Management (₹1.05 trillion), Manipal Health Enterprises (₹91,655 crore) and INDO-MIM (₹63,442 crore).
 
Dhoot Transmission, Zetwerk Manufacturing, Milky Mist Dairy, Lalithaa Jewellery Mart, Shadowfax Technologies, Aequs, Bonfiglioli Transmissions and Molbio Diagnostics added between ₹15,000 crore and ₹33,000 crore of market-cap to the total BSE-listed companies.
 
Calendar year 2027 (CY27), according to Gaurang Shah, senior vice-president, Geojit Financial is likely to be another good year for the primary market. 
ALSO READ: Street signs: Youngest on the Street, IPOs warm up again, and more
 
"A number of issues did well in CY26 even as the secondary markets remained dull. CY27 is likely to be better in terms of the total number of issues and the amount raised if the secondary markets remain buoyant. Which IPOs will succeed will depend how the issues are priced. There will not be any dearth of liquidity if the issues are attractively priced," he said.
 
G Chokkalingam, founder and head of research at Equinomics Research, too, believes liquidity concerns on account of booming IPOs are likely to ease going ahead. However, he remains cautious on the road ahead for the primary markets in case of a sharp correction in the mid-and small-caps.
 
"A meltdown in small-and mid-cap stocks is set to lead to a slowdown in IPOs. Already, the SME fund raising has dropped by 70 per cent sequentially to Rs 643 crore in October. However, the mainboard IPOs raised a huge Rs 44,451 crore in October alone, but Jio accounted for 68 per cent of that. We expect momentum in IPOs to weaken in the immediate short-term even though CY27 looks promising for the secondary market if geopolitical situation and the macros back home remain supportive," he said.
 
SMID snapshot
 
Meanwhile, out of BSE 500 stocks, more than half (286 stocks) are currently trading below their December 1, 2025 levels. The BSE 500 stocks accounted for 85 per cent of the market-cap of BSE-listed companies. The BSE 500 index hit intraday high of 37,449.99 level on Thursday, stood 3.4 per cent shy from its all-time high of 38,740.08 touched on September 27, 2024, exchange data shows.
 
ALSO READ: India's stock market premium faces test from slower growth, tight rates: UBS
Infosys, ITC, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), HCL Technologies, HDFC Bank, Maruti Suzuki India, Hindustan Unilever and Reliance Industries from the Sensex were down in the range of 12.5-30 per cent from December 1, 2025 levels.
 
Among other notable stocks, KPIT Technologies, Swiggy, PI Industries, PB Fintech, Kaynes Technologies, Rail Vikas Nigam, SBI Cards and Payment Services, and Bata India were down between 35-59 per cent.
 
However, seven stocks, HFCL, Aditya Infotech, Ather Energy, Welspun Corp, Laurus Labs, Acutaas Chemicals and Sai Life Sciences saw their market price more than double and appreciated up to 174 per cent from December 2025 levels. 29 other stocks rallied in the range of 50-91 per cent, while another 59 stocks added 25-49 per cent in value, data shows.

data.title: Cyclone Akvan weakens, likely to cross Odisha coast near Gopalpur today
data.description:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Friday said that Cyclone Akvan had weakened into a cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal and is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by forenoon, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph.

According to the IMD, the system moved north-northwestwards at a speed of 21 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred over the westcentral Bay of Bengal at 2:30 AM on Friday.

The cyclonic storm was located near latitude 17.7°N and longitude 84.9°E, about 110 km southeast of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 170 km east of Visakhapatnam, 170 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, 250 km south-southwest of Puri and 370 km east-northeast of Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh.

 

The IMD said the system was likely to continue moving north-northwestwards before crossing the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by forenoon on Friday.

Latest satellite imagery indicated that land interaction had commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with Cyclone Akvan entered the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coastal region.

The weather system is under continuous surveillance by the Doppler Weather Radars at Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur.

Meanwhile, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi spent more than two-and-a-half hours, from around 11 PM to 1:30 AM, at the Special Relief Commissioner's (SRC) office reviewing the evolving situation as the cyclone approached the coast.

During the review, the Chief Minister held direct consultations with officials and directed them to ensure that all necessary assistance reached residents while making every effort to achieve the zero-casualty target.

He returned to his residence at around 1:35 AM amid rainfall.

The pre-landfall impact of Cyclone Akvan began to be felt in Bhubaneswar around 1 AM, with heavy rainfall accompanied by gusty winds. With landfall expected around noon on Thursday, authorities said pre-storm conditions were already affecting the state capital.

Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari, Chief Secretary Anu Garg, Additional Chief Secretary and Revenue Secretary Arabinda Padhee, Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Prabhakar Patil, Fire Services Director General Sudhanshu Sarangi and several senior officials also held discussions with district administrations in cyclone-affected areas.

Most officials remained at their respective offices overnight to monitor the situation and evacuation efforts, including the shifting of residents from vulnerable areas to safer shelters.

data.title: AI sell-off hits Indian smallcaps; Sterlite, HFCL down up to 29% in a month
data.description:
The global sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has also shifted focus to Indian companies linked to the AI ecosystem. According to an analysis by Business Standard, smallcap stocks linked to the US data-centre and AI investment boom have come under significant selling pressure over the past one month, moving in tandem with the Nasdaq Composite index, which has declined 7.5 per cent.
 
Analysts warn that the sharp rally in several such stocks may have left valuations stretched, making them vulnerable to corrections amid the global reassessment of AI-related investments.
 
The stocks under coverage that have delivered handsome returns over the past year have one thing in common -- exposure to the US data-centre boom. These include Sterlite Technologies (STL), HFCL, Aditya Infotech, Sansera Engineering, Acutaas Chemicals, Welspun Corp, Netweb Technologies and MTAR Technologies. 
 
Sterlite Tech, HFCL down up 29% in 1 month 
Exchange data, as of November 18, showed that Sterlite Technologies shares have declined 27 per cent in the past month, although its one year return stood at 481 per cent. Similarly, HFCL shares have fallen 29 per cent in a month but gained 159 per cent over a year.
 
Welspun Corp and MTAR Technologies shares declined 15 per cent and 17 per cent, respectively, over the past month. However, they gained 145 per cent and 130 per cent, respectively, over one year.
 
Netweb Technologies shares have slipped 11 per cent over the past month (up 29 per cent in 1 year). E2E Networks shares have declined 24 per cent in a month but remain up 96 per cent over the past year. 
AI sell-off hits Indian smallcaps
 
Why are AI stocks under pressure? Analysts said that as AI investments face growing scrutiny in the US, concerns over valuations, debt-funded capital expenditure and the sustainability of spending by large technology companies may spill over to Indian companies linked to the global AI and data-centre ecosystem.
 
However, there are few exceptions. Data showed that Aditya Infotech shares remained largely unchanged over the past month, while gaining 133 per cent over one year. Sansera Engineering shares rose 13 per cent in a month and 197 per cent over a year. Acutaas Chemicals gained 22.5 per cent over the past month and its one year return stood at 132 per cent. 
'Anti-AI trade' 
Apoorva Khandelwal, research associate at Anand Rathi Institutional Equities, said the correction in several stocks is largely a reflection of the emerging 'anti-AI trade', as investors become increasingly concerned about debt-funded AI capex, pressure on hyperscalers' free cash flows and rising financing costs. There are also concerns around tighter regulations, power availability and potential delays in data-centre projects in the US, which could slow the pace of AI infrastructure spending.
 
"Indian companies exposed to this theme, particularly in optical fibre and data centre infrastructure, are vulnerable as valuations have already factored in strong growth expectations," he said. Sterlite Tech, HFCL order books
 
The order books of some companies highlight their significant exposure to the AI and data-centre ecosystem. Sterlite Technologies' order book has expanded 4.6-fold since March to about ₹35,274 crore, supported by $1.2 billion (approximately ₹11,400 crore) in deals with hyperscalers, or large cloud and technology companies operating extensive data-centre networks.
 
According to HFCL's management, a large portion of its roughly ₹18,500 crore fibre and data-centre order book comes from hyperscalers. 
'Underlying opportunity intact' 
Despite the recent correction, Vinit Bolinjkar, head of research at Ventura, believes the underlying opportunity remains intact, and that investors should distinguish between companies with direct exposure to AI infrastructure spending and those benefiting indirectly from the broader data-centre investment cycle.
 
He said that Netweb trades at approx 60-65 times trailing earnings, E2E Networks at around 90 times and Black Box at approximately 65 times. "Such multiples leave limited room for execution delays, margin pressure or earnings disappointments," he said.

data.title: EPFO's ₹1,800 crore Reliance Capital loss: Can workers' money be recovered?
data.description:
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has intimated its trustees that it has no further legal course to recover the remaining outstanding amount from Reliance Capital Limited (RCL). The amount is estimated to be ₹1,816 crore, following the company’s insolvency resolution.
 
EPFO had invested ₹2,500 crore in Reliance Capital Limited in the form of non-convertible debentures (NCDs). The company defaulted, and EPFO recovered only ₹1,492.45 crore through the process of insolvency. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a case in August 2026 over an alleged siphoning of the remaining amount.  

How did EPFO invest workers’ retirement savings in Reliance Capital?

Reliance Capital raised money by issuing non-convertible debentures. These are the fixed-income corporate debt instruments issued by companies to raise long-term capital from the public. This is expected to be repaid in principal with interest on maturity.
 
 
EPFO invested ₹2,500 crore in these instruments in 2013-2014 through four portfolio managers. This includes Reliance Capital Asset Management. The debentures were scheduled to mature in 2023-2024. However, RCL defaulted on interest payments from  October 2019, according to the government’s statement in Parliament.

Why has EPFO been unable to recover the remaining ₹1,800 crore?

The Reserve Bank of India started the insolvency proceedings against RCL in 2021. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved a resolution plan submitted by Hinduja Group entity Indusland International Holdings in February 2024. Finally, the takeover was completed in March 2025.
 
The legal discrepancy arises from Section 31 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The NCLT-approved resolution plan binds the company and its creditors towards the proposed mechanism. This implies that creditors cannot raise additional claims after the resolution process is completed.
 
EPFO’s original claim was for ₹2,500 crore, which was the principal amount and ₹808.67 crore in interest. After receiving ₹1,492.45 crore. Now, EPFO says that the completed resolution process prevents further recovery through its original claim.
 
“No, given the claim is as a financial creditor on account of investment made by EPFO, once the resolution plan reaches finality, recourse & legal remedies reach a closure,” said Bikash Jhawar, Senior Partner, Saraf & Partners.
 
EPFO could, however, take action against the old management of Reliance Capital and other people if it believes there is criminality/fraud involved in dealing with its investments but Reliance Capital itself would be insulated from such recourse, Jhawar further added.

Can fraud investigations open another route to recovering the money?

The CBI’s August case raises more legal questions to be merged with this development. It is investigating allegations of fraudulent transactions and diversion of funds that allegedly contributed to RCL’s default. Allegations of cheating, criminal conspiracy and criminal breach of trust.
 
“The recourse under sections 43, 45, 49 or 66 of the IBC is available to the resolution professional (RP) or liquidator of the corporate debtor, would generally not be available to the EPFO as a creditor,” said Ieshan Sinha, Partner, Wadia Ghandy & Co.
 
In this case, the administrator, the RP equivalent for insolvency of corporate debtors who are NBFCs, had already filed proceedings under these sections and recoveries were accounted for in the resolution plan. If some further fraud or illegality is uncovered by pending investigation in relation to EPFO’s claims, it may be more feasible for EPFO to pursue appropriate civil proceedings, Sinha added further.
 
Section 66 deals with fraudulent or wrongful trading.
 
However, investigating fraud does not automatically reopen an approved resolution plan; first, it needs to be proved. Section 32A also protects a corporate debtor from being prosecuted for certain offences committed before insolvency, once an eligible new management takes control.
 
“In Piramal Capital v. 63 Moons Technologies, the Supreme Court recognised that avoidance proceedings need not automatically abate upon plan approval, provided their prosecution and distribution are lawfully preserved,” said Rohit Jain, Managing Partner, Singhania & Co.

Who was responsible for monitoring EPFO’s investments and managing the risks?

Portfolio managers are responsible for EPFO’s debt investments. These managers are appointed by its Central Board of Trustees. They must adhere to the government's investment patterns and EPFO’s investment guidelines.
 
These guidelines require investment decisions to prioritise safety, prudence and reasonable returns. EPFO also uses external auditors and performance benchmarks to monitor portfolio managers.

Does the loss affect workers’ provident fund balances or future returns?

The loss does not automatically mean that individual EPF accounts will be debited or that workers must repay the amount. Under Paragraph 60 of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952, interest is credited to members’ accounts at a rate determined by the Central Government in consultation with the Central Board of Trustees.
 
“The finality of a resolution plan does not confer immunity upon individuals responsible for fraudulent transactions,” said Shiv Sapra, Partner, Kochhar & Co.
 
While recovery against the resolved corporate debtor remains constrained, proceedings against persons involved in fraud may survive, subject to the statutory framework. Crucially, any recovery would depend on establishing wrongdoing and identifying a legally sustainable remedy, rather than merely proving that EPFO suffered a loss, Sapra further added.
